q: what is the human body made of
a: The human body is composed mostly of water (about 60%), along with proteins, fats, minerals (calcium, phosphorus, potassium), and carbohydrates. At the elemental level, the body is mostly oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen.

q: how many bones are in the human body
how many bones do humans have
a: The adult human body has 206 bones. Babies are born with about 270 bones, but some fuse together as they grow.

q: what is the largest organ in the human body
a: The skin is the largest organ in the human body, with an average surface area of about 1.5 to 2 square meters (16 to 22 square feet).

q: how much blood is in the human body
a: The average adult human body contains about 4.5 to 5.5 liters (1.2 to 1.5 gallons) of blood, which makes up about 7-8% of total body weight.

q: what percentage of the human body is water
a: The human body is approximately 60% water. However, this varies by age and gender: infants are about 75% water, adult men about 60%, and adult women about 55%.

q: what is the strongest muscle in the human body
a: The masseter (jaw muscle) is the strongest muscle by force. The gluteus maximus (buttock) is the largest muscle. The heart is the hardest-working muscle, beating about 100,000 times per day.

q: how fast do brain signals travel
how fast do nerves transmit signals
a: Nerve impulses in the human body can travel at speeds up to 120 meters per second (268 mph), though the speed varies depending on the type of nerve fiber and whether it is myelinated.
